analysis.title: The volatility trap: From panic to FOMO in less than a week
key_insights: VIX fell from 28 to 20 in roughly 2.5 sessions. Dealers bought back short delta as vol dropped, which fed a self-reinforcing equity rally. When the vol crush stalled, the rally stalled too (Nomura, McElligott).

Thursday's selloff saw SPX fall 4.4% and NDX fall 6.4%, with VIX up 11.6 points in one session. BofA says it was one of the most extreme intraday drawdowns relative to overnight performance since 2008. The VIX shock was comparable to Feb 2018 and Aug 2024.
BofA attributes the crash mainly to positioning and reflexive feedback loops rather than fundamentals, calling it a market structure accident and not necessarily a fundamental breakdown.
The VIX overshoot from Thursday has normalized. The gap between VIX and SPX is basically closed.
The VIX term structure reset at the short end. Short-term hedges bought in panic were hit by the rebound and the repricing of short-dated vol.
Vol-control funds cut exposure as vol rose. If realized vol keeps drifting lower, Nomura expects the vol-control bid to return gradually, turning the flows that amplified the selloff into a tailwind.

BofA says the one-month performance spread between defensives and technology is at extremes last seen in the dotcom era. The defensive trade is vulnerable to a sharp reversal, and the report sees conditions for a tech squeeze, with defensives underperforming as the next pain trade.
BofA says US tech is on track for its second most fragile year in over three decades, behind only 2025. Earnings reactions are getting more violent without a matching deterioration in fundamentals.

Nomura puts leveraged ETF assets at about $142B (near the 94th percentile), with about $6.5B of rebalancing exposure per 1% market move (near the 95th percentile). Together with vol-targeting strategies and options flows, this raises the potential for self-reinforcing moves in either direction.

Nomura's McElligott says 10- and 20-day realized volatility of VVIX are at record highs on a 10-year lookback, above COVID, Liberation Day and Volmageddon. He warns of a regime of more violent two-way moves with a structurally higher VIX floor.

Morgan Stanley's Privorotsky says rising yields are a headwind but equities have a cushion. Another leg higher in rates would be more problematic, especially if oil keeps inflation sticky and the Fed hawkish. Credit spreads are the key risk gauge.

Morgan Stanley notes gross exposure has been cut, net positioning is historically low and vol is still elevated, which leaves room for a squeeze as vol decays. The market is still one vol shock away from reversing the feedback loop.

sector_views.rationale: BofA flags an extreme defensives-vs-tech performance spread and a reset in positioning and volatility, which sets up a possible tech squeeze.
BofA says the rush into defensives is stretched and vulnerable to a violent reversal, with defensives underperforming as tech rebounds the next pain trade.

earnings_insights: BofA says earnings reactions in US tech are becoming more violent even though fundamentals have not deteriorated at the same pace.

macro_indicators.interpretation: One of the most extreme intraday drawdowns relative to overnight performance since 2008. BofA attributes it to positioning and feedback loops.
The plunge in tech was larger than the broad index decline, consistent with fragile tech positioning.
The vol collapse triggered dealer hedging flows that supported the equity rebound.

risk_factors: Another vol shock could reverse the feedback loop that is supporting the rebound (Morgan Stanley).
Higher yields, especially another leg higher in rates, with oil keeping inflation sticky and the Fed hawkish (Morgan Stanley).
Widening credit spreads, which Morgan Stanley calls the key risk gauge.
Record realized VVIX volatility points to unstable vol and possible violent two-way moves (Nomura).
Leveraged ETF rebalancing and vol-targeting flows can amplify moves in either direction.
A sharp reversal of the crowded defensive trade (BofA).
vol_and_positioning: VIX dropped from 28 to 20 in about 2.5 sessions. It had risen 11.6 points in one session on Thursday. The VIX-to-SPX gap has closed.
The short end of the VIX term structure reset sharply, and short-dated hedges bought in panic lost value in the rebound.
Dealers bought back short delta as vol fell. The rally stalled when the vol crush stalled.
Vol-control funds cut exposure in the spike and could re-add if realized vol keeps drifting lower.
Realized volatility of VVIX over 10 and 20 days is at record highs on a 10-year lookback, above COVID, Liberation Day and Volmageddon (Nomura).
Nomura sees a structurally higher VIX floor and more violent two-way moves.
Leveraged ETF assets are about $142B (94th percentile), with about $6.5B of rebalancing exposure per 1% market move (95th percentile).

tension_points.bull_case: Gross exposure is cut, net positioning is historically low and vol is decaying, which leaves room for a squeeze (Morgan Stanley). Vol-control funds could re-add if realized vol drifts lower (Nomura). A defensives-to-tech reversal could drive a tech squeeze (BofA).
tension_points.bear_case: Record realized VVIX volatility signals unstable vol and a structurally higher VIX floor (Nomura). Rising yields with sticky oil-driven inflation and a hawkish Fed are a headwind (Morgan Stanley). The rebound was mechanical, and the rally stalled when the vol crush stalled.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another volatility shock, or a further leg higher in rates, which Morgan Stanley says would reverse the feedback loop. Credit spreads are the gauge Morgan Stanley names as the key risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: Dealer hedging, vol-control re-leveraging and low positioning are driving the rebound as vol decays.
theme_stances.evidence: Positioning is the tailwind. The Fed remains the headwind.

theme_stances.key_argument: The defensives-versus-tech spread is at dotcom-era extremes, and a violent reversal could squeeze tech.
theme_stances.evidence: The next pain trade could be defensives underperforming as tech comes roaring back.

theme_stances.key_argument: Realized volatility of VVIX is at record highs, pointing to violent two-way moves and a higher VIX floor.
theme_stances.evidence: The volatility of volatility itself is becoming unstable.
